diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed all four decisive facts (PF1–PF4) and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed (1 of 4 passed) due to ENCODING MISMATCH issues across three rollouts. In rollout 0, C3 failed because the settlement encoded network_configuration as "District-secure IoT network with wired drops" (capital D) while C3 expects lowercase "district-secure". In rollout 2, C5, C6, and C7 all failed because the model used generic commitment types and role-based targets ("facility_upgrade"/"facilities", "network_configuration"/"IT", "financial_record"/"finance") instead of the specific commitment types and named-agent targets that those checks require (as evidenced by the passing rollout 1, which used "infrastructure_upgrade"/"Mr. Ortiz", "network_installation"/"Ms. Shah", and "fund_documentation"/"Mr. Greene"). In rollout 3, C1 failed because the model chose conversion_approved=false (conditional approval with precedents) while C1 appears to require conversion_approved=true alongside student_workstations=16, even though the workstation count itself was correctly set to 16.

C6.why: The vendor specification changes the network choice from unspecified or ordinary Wi-Fi to the district-secure IoT network with wired drops and requires an installation commitment.

C5.why: The inspection changes the infrastructure decision from using the existing circuit to installing a dedicated 240-volt circuit and documenting that upgrade.

C3.why: The vendor specification changes the network choice from unspecified or ordinary Wi-Fi to the district-secure IoT network with wired drops and requires an installation commitment.

C1.why: The confirmed roster changes the approved workstation count from the draft 12 to exactly 16.

C7.why: The executed award changes the funding entry to exactly $18,500 from the workforce-development grant and requires the amount to be recorded in the project ledger.

Enter the $18,500 workforce-development grant award notice into the project ledger to fully document the funding source for the vendor.
Confirm that the combined cost estimates from Mr. Ortiz and Ms. Shah fit within the $18,500 grant restriction before final approval.
Update the conversion request to reflect 16 student workstations, the dedicated 240-volt circuit requirement, and the district-secure IoT network with wired drops before resubmission.

transcript.speaker: A1

fix_instructions: Fix C3 to be case-insensitive on the network_configuration field, or normalize the expected value to accept both "District-secure" and "district-secure" capitalizations — this drove the rollout 0 failure. Fix C5, C6, and C7 to match on commitment detail content rather than exact commitment type strings or target names, since the model naturally varies between specific types like "infrastructure_upgrade"/"Mr. Ortiz" and generic types like "facility_upgrade"/"facilities" while conveying the same action — this drove the rollout 2 failures. Fix C1 to check only that student_workstations equals 16 (the factual outcome of PF1) rather than also requiring conversion_approved=true, since a conditional-approval decision with correct workstation count is a valid use of PF1 — this drove the rollout 3 failure. No changes to shared_context or agent personalities are needed; all facts were reliably revealed and cited in every rollout.
